title: FORGE KB MCP Server: Unified Bedrock KB Gateway
description: Centralizes all Bedrock Knowledge Base operations across FIP apps through a unified MCP server. Replaces scattered bedrock-agent-runtime calls in FIRM, NEXUS, and FAIT v1 with a single authenticated endpoint that handles KB search, ingest, and metadata operations over HTTP/SSE transport.

parentTitle: FORGE KB MCP Server: Unified Bedrock KB Gateway

description: Sets up the foundational Node.js MCP server with HTTP/SSE transport, ECR deployment pipeline, and ECS service configuration on fortress-tools-cluster. Provides the technical foundation for all KB tools.
acceptanceCriteria:

- [ ] ECR repository fip-mcp created with standard lifecycle policy

title: As a system architect, I want an ECS service fip-mcp deployed on fortress-tools-cluster so that the MCP server runs as a managed Fargate service
description:
## ECS Service Creation
**Resource:** fip-mcp ECS service on fortress-tools-cluster
**Purpose:** Runs the MCP server as a managed Fargate container service
**Configuration:**
- Service name: fip-mcp
- Cluster: fortress-tools-cluster
- Launch type: Fargate
- vCPU: 0.25 (256)
- Memory: 512 MB
- Desired count: 1 (always-on)
- Container port: 3000
- Task execution role with Bedrock permissions (see IAM story)
**Verification:** Service shows as RUNNING in ECS console with 1/1 tasks healthy
acceptanceCriteria:
- [ ] ECS service fip-mcp exists on fortress-tools-cluster
- [ ] Fargate launch type with 0.25 vCPU / 512MB configuration
- [ ] Desired count set to 1 for always-on availability
- [ ] Container port 3000 exposed for ALB targeting
- [ ] Service successfully pulls from ECR fip-mcp repository

title: As a cloud engineer, I want ALB target group and routing rule configured so that api.fortressam.ai/mcp/* routes to fip-mcp service
description:
## ALB Target Group Configuration
**Resource:** ALB target group for fip-mcp service
**Purpose:** Routes CloudFlare traffic from api.fortressam.ai/mcp/* to the MCP server container
**Configuration:**
- Target group name: fip-mcp-tg
- Target type: IP (Fargate)
- Protocol: HTTP
- Port: 3000 (or container port from ECS service)
- Health check path: /health
- Host-based routing rule: Host = api.fortressam.ai AND path starts with /mcp
**Verification:** GET request to https://api.fortressam.ai/health returns 200 OK through the full CF → ALB → ECS chain
acceptanceCriteria:
- [ ] ALB target group fip-mcp-tg created and targets ECS service
- [ ] Routing rule forwards api.fortressam.ai/mcp/* to fip-mcp target group
- [ ] Health check configured on /health endpoint
- [ ] Target group shows healthy targets when ECS service is running

title: Implement Entra OAuth Authentication
description: Validates Entra OAuth bearer tokens on all MCP endpoints using JWKS signature verification. Extracts user identity claims (oid, groups, roles) for KB scoping and entitlement enforcement. Provides the security foundation for all KB operations.
acceptanceCriteria:
- [ ] Every request to /mcp and /mcp/sse validates Authorization: Bearer JWT header
- [ ] Token signature verified against Entra JWKS endpoint
- [ ] aud claim matches ENTRA_CLIENT_ID environment variable
- [ ] tid claim matches ENTRA_TENANT_ID environment variable
- [ ] Expired tokens rejected with 401
- [ ] Missing or invalid tokens rejected with 401
- [ ] Valid tokens extract oid, groups, and roles claims for use by tools
- [ ] /health endpoint bypasses authentication (no token required)

title: As a security engineer, I want JWT token validation middleware implemented so that only authenticated users can access MCP endpoints
description:
## Developer Brief — JWT Token Validation
**Spec Reference:** Section 4
### Context
Every MCP endpoint request must validate the Entra OAuth bearer token to ensure only authenticated FIP users can access KB operations.
### Scope
JWT validation middleware using Entra JWKS endpoint for signature verification and claim validation
### Technical Notes
- Use jsonwebtoken + jwks-rsa or @azure/msal-node for validation
- Cache JWKS keys for performance
- Extract oid, groups, roles claims for downstream use
- Middleware applies to /mcp and /mcp/sse only - /health bypasses auth
### Dependencies
ENTRA_TENANT_ID and ENTRA_CLIENT_ID from Secrets Manager
### Open Questions
None
acceptanceCriteria:
- [ ] Middleware validates Authorization: Bearer JWT header on every /mcp and /mcp/sse request
- [ ] Token signature verified against Entra JWKS endpoint with key caching
- [ ] aud claim validated against ENTRA_CLIENT_ID environment variable
- [ ] tid claim validated against ENTRA_TENANT_ID environment variable
- [ ] Expired tokens return 401 Unauthorized
- [ ] Missing Authorization header returns 401 Unauthorized
- [ ] Invalid token signature returns 401 Unauthorized
- [ ] Valid tokens populate request context with oid, groups, and roles claims
- [ ] /health endpoint accessible without token
testedByTitles: TC: Given valid JWT with correct aud/tid claims, When request to /mcp, Then token validated and claims extracted
TC: Given expired JWT, When request to /mcp, Then returns 401 Unauthorized
TC: Given missing Authorization header, When request to /mcp, Then returns 401 Unauthorized
TC: Given request to /health endpoint, When no Authorization header, Then returns 200 OK bypassing auth

title: As a security engineer, I want KB auto-scoping filters enforced so that users can only access their authorized KB content
description:
## Developer Brief — KB Auto-Scoping Security
**Spec Reference:** Section 3.1, Section 4
### Context
Security-enforced filter injection ensures users can only access KB content they are authorized to see. Cannot be overridden by caller-supplied filters.
### Scope
Automatic filter injection for Personal, Team, and Project KBs based on token claims
### Technical Notes
Server merges auto-injected filters with caller filters using AND logic. Auto-scoping is mandatory security enforcement.
### Dependencies
JWT token validation and team_memberships table (once available)
### Open Questions
Team membership validation implementation when team_memberships table not yet available
acceptanceCriteria:
- [ ] Personal KB (ZCEZCJGHQC, PBKCTCPNUU) auto-injects user_id = token.oid filter
- [ ] Team KB requires team_id in caller filters and validates membership via team_memberships lookup
- [ ] Project KB requires project_id in caller filters and validates project access
- [ ] Corp KB (WYSKBKWHPL, AOFDTSHGNT) and NEXUS KB (WHB6WU9CVW) have no auto-scoping
- [ ] Auto-injected filters cannot be overridden by caller-supplied filters
- [ ] Filter merging uses AND logic between auto-injected and caller filters
- [ ] Missing team_id for Team KB returns 400 PROJECT_ID_REQUIRED error
- [ ] Invalid team membership returns 403 PROJECT_ACCESS_DENIED error
testedByTitles: TC: Given Personal KB search with token.oid=user123, When search_kb called, Then auto-injects user_id=user123 filter
TC: Given Team KB search without team_id, When search_kb called, Then returns 400 PROJECT_ID_REQUIRED
TC: Given Team KB search with invalid team membership, When search_kb called, Then returns 403 PROJECT_ACCESS_DENIED
TC: Given Corp KB search, When search_kb called, Then no auto-scoping filters applied

title: As a FAIT v2 agent, I want search_kb tool implemented so that I can perform semantic searches across FORGE Knowledge Bases
description:
## Developer Brief — search_kb Tool Implementation
**Spec Reference:** Section 3.1
### Context
Core MCP tool for semantic KB retrieval using bedrock-agent-runtime:Retrieve API with security-enforced auto-scoping.
### Scope
JSON-RPC tool accepting query, kb_id, top_k, and optional filters with Bedrock API integration
### Technical Notes
- Use @aws-sdk/client-bedrock-agent-runtime for Retrieve calls
- Auto-scope filters based on KB type per security rules
- Merge caller filters with auto-injected security filters using AND logic
- Return relevance scores 0.0-1.0 from Bedrock response
### Dependencies
Bedrock IAM permissions and KB auto-scoping implementation
### Open Questions
None
acceptanceCriteria:
- [ ] Tool accepts query (required), kb_id (required), top_k (optional, default 5), filters (optional)
- [ ] kb_id validated against KB inventory from spec
- [ ] Calls bedrock-agent-runtime:Retrieve with proper parameters
- [ ] Auto-scoping filters injected based on KB type and token claims
- [ ] Returns array of results with content, metadata, and relevance_score
- [ ] Error handling: UNKNOWN_KB (400), NOT_ENTITLED (403), PROJECT_ID_REQUIRED (400), PROJECT_ACCESS_DENIED (403)
- [ ] Tool registered in MCP server tool list

title: As a client application, I want list_kbs tool implemented so that I can discover which Knowledge Bases the current user can access
description:

JSON-RPC tool querying entitlements and returning filtered KB list with metadata
### Technical Notes
- Check DB table first, fall back to static config
- NEXUS KB always readable for authenticated users
- Include kb_type, description, and writable flag in response
- Filter by user's entitlements and group memberships
### Dependencies
Entitlement system (DB table or fallback config)
### Open Questions
None
acceptanceCriteria:
- [ ] Tool queries kb_entitlements table when DB available
- [ ] Falls back to FALLBACK_ENTITLEMENTS_CONFIG when DB unavailable
- [ ] Returns array of entitled KBs with kb_id, kb_type, description, writable fields
- [ ] NEXUS KB (WHB6WU9CVW) always included as readable for authenticated users
- [ ] Group membership from token.groups adds additional entitlements
- [ ] Default entitlements applied to all authenticated users
- [ ] Tool registered in MCP server tool list

title: As a FIRM backend, I want add_to_kb tool implemented so that I can ingest meeting summaries into Personal KB asynchronously
description:
## Developer Brief — add_to_kb Tool Implementation
**Spec Reference:** Section 3.3
### Context
Async content ingestion tool using bedrock-agent-runtime:StartIngestionJob. Replaces direct Bedrock calls in FIRM's summarization pipeline.
### Scope
JSON-RPC tool for KB content ingestion with write entitlement validation and async job tracking
### Technical Notes
- Validate write entitlement before ingestion
- Require metadata.source and metadata.created_by fields
- Return job_id immediately for polling with get_job_status
- Use StartIngestionJob API or S3 trigger (Tony to determine based on KB setup)
### Dependencies
Bedrock IAM permissions and write entitlement validation
### Open Questions
S3 trigger vs direct StartIngestionJob implementation approach
acceptanceCriteria:
- [ ] Tool accepts kb_id (required), content (required), metadata (required)
- [ ] Validates user has write entitlement for target KB
- [ ] Validates metadata includes source and created_by fields
- [ ] Project KB requires metadata.project_id field
- [ ] Calls bedrock-agent-runtime:StartIngestionJob or equivalent S3 trigger
- [ ] Returns status: queued, job_id, and kb_id immediately
- [ ] Error handling: WRITE_NOT_ENTITLED (403), METADATA_REQUIRED (400), PROJECT_ID_REQUIRED (400)
- [ ] Tool registered in MCP server tool list

title: As a monitoring system, I want get_kb_metadata tool implemented so that I can retrieve KB statistics and configuration
description:
## Developer Brief — get_kb_metadata Tool Implementation
**Spec Reference:** Section 3.4
### Context
Provides KB stats and config info using GetKnowledgeBase and ListIngestionJobs APIs for monitoring and admin purposes.
### Scope
JSON-RPC tool returning KB metadata with document count, last updated timestamp, and data source ID
### Technical Notes
- Use GetKnowledgeBase for basic info and data_source_id
- Use ListIngestionJobs to derive last_updated from most recent completed job
- Require read entitlement for the target KB
- Return ISO 8601 timestamp format
### Dependencies
Bedrock IAM permissions and read entitlement validation
### Open Questions
None
acceptanceCriteria:
- [ ] Tool accepts kb_id (required)
- [ ] Validates user has read entitlement for target KB
- [ ] Calls bedrock-agent-runtime:GetKnowledgeBase for basic metadata
- [ ] Calls bedrock-agent-runtime:ListIngestionJobs to derive last_updated
- [ ] Returns kb_id, kb_type, document_count, last_updated (ISO 8601), data_source_id
- [ ] Error handling: UNKNOWN_KB (400), NOT_ENTITLED (403)
- [ ] Tool registered in MCP server tool list

title: As any FIP MCP client, I want get_job_status tool implemented so that I can poll the status of asynchronous operations
description:
## Developer Brief — get_job_status Tool Implementation
**Spec Reference:** Section 3.5
### Context
Universal async polling tool for FIP MCP servers. For KB jobs, calls GetIngestionJob. Establishes the pattern for future async tools.
### Scope
JSON-RPC tool for job status polling with support for KB ingestion jobs and extensible job type routing
### Technical Notes
- For MVP, in-memory job tracking is acceptable (single container, rare restarts)
- Route KB job IDs to bedrock-agent-runtime:GetIngestionJob
- Return standard status enum: queued, running, complete, failed
- Include result/error/percent_complete when available
### Dependencies
Bedrock IAM permissions for GetIngestionJob
### Open Questions
None
acceptanceCriteria:
- [ ] Tool accepts job_id (required)
- [ ] Routes KB ingestion job IDs to bedrock-agent-runtime:GetIngestionJob
- [ ] Returns status enum: queued, running, complete, failed
- [ ] Includes result object when status = complete
- [ ] Includes error string when status = failed
- [ ] Includes percent_complete (0-100) when available
- [ ] Job tracking system (in-memory for MVP) maps job_id to backend APIs
- [ ] Tool registered in MCP server tool list

title: As a web client developer, I want CORS headers configured so that browser-based FIP applications can make cross-origin requests to the MCP server
description:
## Developer Brief — CORS Configuration
**Spec Reference:** Section 2
### Context
FIP applications run on different domains (Azure for FAIT v2, AWS for others). Browser CORS policy requires proper headers for cross-origin MCP requests with authentication.
### Scope
Server-side CORS header configuration supporting known FIP origins with credentialed requests
### Technical Notes
- Cannot use wildcard (*) origin with credentialed requests
- Must explicitly list fortressam.ai subdomains
- CloudFlare must pass headers through unmodified
- Support preflight OPTIONS requests
### Dependencies
None - server-side implementation
### Open Questions
Complete list of FIP subdomain origins to support
acceptanceCriteria:
- [ ] CORS middleware allows origins: https://fait.dev.fortressam.ai, https://fait.fortressam.ai, https://firm.dev.fortressam.ai, https://nexus.fortressam.ai
- [ ] Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true set for authenticated requests
- [ ] Access-Control-Allow-Headers includes Authorization, Content-Type
- [ ] Access-Control-Allow-Methods includes GET, POST, OPTIONS
- [ ] Preflight OPTIONS requests handled properly
- [ ] No wildcard (*) origins used with credentialed requests
- [ ] CORS headers set by server, not modified by CloudFlare

title: TC: Given Corp KB search, When search_kb called, Then no auto-scoping filters applied
description:
**Given:** Search request to Corp KB (org-wide access)
**When:** search_kb tool called
**Then:** No auto-scoping filters injected, only caller-supplied filters used
